title: Borsuk delivery is documented for an earlier contract while SAFE lists a separate later contract scope
source_unit: Polish Ministry of National Defence Borsuk and SAFE program pages
geography: Poland; Polish Armed Forces and Polish defense industry

denominator.unit: Borsuk infantry fighting vehicles in the March 2025 executive contract

first_serial_delivery.unit: vehicles handed over to the Polish Armed Forces

delivery_window.unit: planned delivery years for the 111-vehicle contract

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official Polish Ministry of National Defence Borsuk program and contract pages. The 15-vehicle handover is retained as a product-level delivery event tied by the source to the earlier 111-vehicle contract.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not provide the full vehicle serial list, acceptance protocol, exact unit location, production-workforce measure, or a connection to the later SAFE contract. Delivery is not the same as operational employment or full capability.
observations.subgroup: Borsuk vehicles under the March 2025 executive contract with PGZ and Huta Stalowa Wola.
observations.counterinterpretation: A first delivery demonstrates realized output for one contract while leaving remaining production, sustainment, local-content control, and operational availability unresolved.

denominator.unit: Borsuk vehicles listed in the SAFE-financed contract scope

safe_contract_stage.value: signed contract scope; no SAFE-specific delivery or acceptance in the cited source

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official MON SAFE program page. The 146-vehicle figure is retained as the later SAFE contract scope and is not pooled with the earlier 111-vehicle contract or its 15 reported deliveries.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not disclose a SAFE contract identifier, delivery schedule, obligation/payment record, acceptance, serial output, or vehicle-level link to the 15 units delivered under the earlier contract.
observations.subgroup: Borsuk scope listed among SAFE-financed contracts with the Polish defense industry.
observations.counterinterpretation: A same-product contract can expand expected demand without proving incremental production, delivery timing, domestic content, or operational availability.

related_sources.claim: Normalized note preserves the earlier delivery, later SAFE scope, and non-pooling boundary.
The SAFE contracting record supplies the broader legislative and domestic-contracting context.
MON supplies the Borsuk contract and first 15-vehicle delivery observation.
MON supplies the later 146-vehicle SAFE contract scope.

boundary: This is a stage-compatible same-product comparison, not a pooled delivery estimate. It establishes one earlier Borsuk delivery and a separate later SAFE contract scope. It does not establish delivery or acceptance of the SAFE-funded 146 vehicles, production increment, local-content share, operational use, public reception, or geopolitical leverage.
